section_summary: This section contains multiple duplicate file copies of Embassy Tokyo's registers of outgoing despatches and telegrams for January 1941, followed by a State Department analysis and Tokyo Despatch No. 5372 enclosing Monthly Report No. 1672 for January 1941. The documents record the escalating tensions in Japanese-American relations following President Roosevelt's speeches, congressional introduction of the Lend-Lease Bill, and Foreign Minister Matsuoka's aggressive policy statements before the Imperial Diet. Key subjects covered include Japan's commitments under the Tripartite Pact, German efforts to provoke conflict between the United States and Japan, regional developments in Southeast Asia including Japanese mediation in the Thai-Indochina border conflict, and local diplomatic friction such as the Peiping Marine-Gendarme incident.

subfiles.about: Continuation of a typed list of despatches forwarded by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: Lists Despatches 5275-5335 (January 1941): Thai Indochina claims, Tripartite adherents Romania/Hungary/Slovakia, German Pacific raiders, and the Imperial Rule Assistance Association's structure.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 1, Pages 2-5)

subfiles.about: Chronological log of telegrams (Nos. 1 through 151) transmitted by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the State Department during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A seven-page registry of telegrams sent by the Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State throughout January 1941. It records telegram numbers, dates, times of dispatch, and brief descriptive subject lines. Important topics indexed include Japanese press reactions to Roosevelt's speeches, Matsuoka's foreign policy pronouncements, Thai-Indochina border clashes and Japanese mediation, the Peiping Marine incident, and British-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, January 1941 (Copy 1)

subfiles.about: Complete duplicate copy of the list of despatches (Nos. 5261 to 5335) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A complete five-page copy of the monthly register of despatches sent from Tokyo to Washington during January 1941. Numbered 5261 through 5335, the despatches report on economic and financial conditions, Japanese press sentiment, bombing damage to American missionary properties in China, and regional Axis diplomatic maneuvers. This represents the second copy of the despatch log included in the file.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 2)

subfiles.about: Second copy of the chronological registry of telegrams (Nos. 1 through 151) dispatched by the American Embassy in Tokyo in January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate seven-page inventory of telegrams transmitted by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the State Department in January 1941. It details outgoing cable communications numbered 1 to 151 with dates, times, and subject titles. Major subjects logged include Japanese mediation in the Thai-Indochinese conflict, Diet interpellations on foreign policy, and reactions to U.S. naval developments.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, January 1941 (Copy 2)

subfiles.about: Third copy of the monthly list of despatches (Nos. 5261 to 5335) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A third five-page copy of the Embassy's despatch index covering serials 5261 to 5335 forwarded during January 1941. The list outlines diplomatic reporting on Japanese domestic politics, treaties, commercial matters, and consular administration. It duplicates the contents of the earlier despatch lists in the multi-copy distribution.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 3)

subfiles.about: Third copy of the chronological log of telegrams (Nos. 1 through 151) sent from Tokyo to Washington in January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A seven-page duplicate record of telegrams dispatched by the Tokyo Embassy to the State Department during January 1941. It chronicles cables 1 through 151, detailing diplomatic exchanges, press digests, and regional security reports. The document matches the previous copies filed in the bundle.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, January 1941 (Copy 3)

subfiles.about: Fourth copy of the list of despatches (Nos. 5261 to 5335) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A five-page duplicate copy of the list of despatches sent from the Embassy in Tokyo to Washington during January 1941. It encompasses despatches numbered 5261 through 5335, providing date and subject entries for reports on political, economic, and administrative affairs. It forms part of the sextuplicate filing of Embassy records.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 4)

subfiles.about: Fourth copy of the list of telegrams (Nos. 1 through 151) sent to the Department of State in January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate seven-page cable register listing telegrams 1 through 151 sent from Tokyo to Washington in January 1941. The log details date, hour of transmission, and subjects such as Diet proceedings, Thai-Indochina armistice efforts, and diplomatic protests. It duplicates earlier copies in the file.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, January 1941 (Copy 4)

subfiles.about: Fifth copy of the list of despatches (Nos. 5261 to 5335) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A five-page duplicate copy of the Tokyo Embassy's despatch register for January 1941, covering numbers 5261 through 5335. Entries outline diplomatic despatches on Japanese internal politics, naval affairs, economic surveys, and missionary property damage in China. It is identical in text to the other copies.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 5)

subfiles.about: Fifth copy of the list of telegrams (Nos. 1 through 151) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A seven-page duplicate listing of outgoing telegrams from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the State Department during January 1941, numbered 1 to 151. It provides details on cable traffic regarding Japanese foreign relations, internal politics, and consular affairs. It forms part of the multi-copy distribution to the Department.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, January 1941 (Copy 5)

subfiles.about: Sixth copy of the list of despatches (Nos. 5261 to 5335) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo during January 1941.
subfiles.summary: A five-page duplicate list of despatches Nos. 5261 through 5335 dispatched by the American Embassy in Tokyo in January 1941. It records serial numbers, dates, and subjects of diplomatic despatches forwarded to Washington. It represents the final duplicate copy of the despatch index in this archival file.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of January 1941 (Copy 6)

subfiles.about: State Department internal memorandum summarizing key findings of Tokyo Despatch No. 5372 regarding conditions in Japan during January 1941.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (initials: OJL)
subfiles.summary: Fales reviews Despatch 5218 (January 1941): Japan's 100-million population goal by 1960, the ¥8.863 billion budget, bond absorption, and economic strain from controls, Western tension, and export limits.
subfiles.title: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 5372

subfiles.about: Covering diplomatic despatch forwarding Report No. 1672 on conditions in Japan during January 1941.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch 5372 transmits Report 1672 on January 1941 Japan conditions in sextuplicate to regional posts.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5372: Transmitting Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan for January 1941

subfiles.about: First ten pages and table of contents of Embassy Tokyo's comprehensive monthly political and economic report on Japan for January 1941.
subfiles.summary: The opening portion of Tokyo Embassy Report No. 1672 surveying conditions in Japan during January 1941, comprising the title page, table of contents, and pages 1 through 10 of the body. It analyzes the acute deterioration in Japanese-American relations, bitter Japanese press denunciations of Roosevelt's fireside chat and the Lend-Lease Bill, and Foreign Minister Matsuoka's assertive statements before the Diet regarding the Western Pacific and the Tripartite Alliance. The text also reviews German efforts to provoke conflict between Japan and the United States, diplomatic friction over American rights in China, the Peiping Marine-Gendarme confrontation, and the detention of the M.S. Estelle L.
subfiles.title: Report No. 1672: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of January, 1941 (Pages 1-10)
